title: Register bounds imply a valid guard
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ be a Boolean-valued function on four indices and finite Boolean words, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean word. If all eighteen registers of a state $\mathrm{st}$ are at most $B$, then for every label $\ell$ the abstract configuration with label $\ell$, register values given by $\mathrm{st}$, and no answer satisfies the guard for the program $A_E$ and input $x$: its registers are bounded by $B$, and its instruction satisfies the guard precondition.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle assigning a Boolean to each of four indices and finite Boolean words
Every register of $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ be an oracle on four indices and bit strings,
let $x$ be a bit string, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a register state whose eighteen
registers are all at most $B$. For every program label $\ell$, the configuration with
label $\ell$, register values given by $\mathrm{st}$, and no answer satisfies the guard:
its registers are bounded by $B$ and its instruction meets the guard's precondition.
